senses.definition: To be at an event or go regularly to a place such as school.
senses.example: We plan to attend the concert on Friday.

senses.definition: The act of looking, listening, or thinking closely about something.
senses.example: The little bird caught my attention when it landed on the fence.

senses.definition: Listening or watching carefully, especially to notice what a person needs.
senses.example: The attentive coach noticed I had missed the directions.

senses.definition: A space or room just under the roof of a building.
senses.example: We found old holiday decorations in the attic.

senses.definition: To draw something or someone toward another thing.
senses.example: The magnet can attract a steel paper clip.

senses.definition: To get people to look at, visit, or care about something.
senses.example: The bright sign might attract more readers to our book table.

senses.definition: A feature or quality that belongs to a person or thing.
senses.example: One attribute of the coat is its large hood.

senses.definition: To say something was caused, made, or said by a certain person or thing.
senses.example: The reporter attributed the delay to the snow.

senses.definition: The people who watch, read, or listen to a performance, story, or message.
senses.example: The audience clapped when the play ended.

senses.definition: A sister of one of your parents or the wife of one of their siblings.
senses.example: My aunt taught me how to make paper stars.

senses.definition: A glow in a planet’s upper atmosphere caused by particles giving energy to a gas there.
senses.example: An aurora looked like a green curtain over the dark hills.

senses.definition: Really what it is said to be, such as an original object.
senses.example: The museum showed us an authentic ticket from the first game.

senses.definition: A person who writes a book, story, or other work.
senses.example: The author chose a dog as the main character.

senses.definition: A person’s name written by that person, often given as a keepsake.
senses.example: The singer wrote an autograph on my ticket.

senses.definition: To sign something with your own name.
senses.example: The book’s author agreed to autograph my copy.

senses.definition: Working or happening by itself once it has been set up.
senses.example: An automatic light turns on when someone walks up to the door.

senses.definition: The season between summer and winter.
senses.example: In autumn, many trees lose their leaves.

senses.definition: Ready to be used, taken, or talked to.
senses.example: Three computers are available at the library today.

senses.definition: A mass of snow that suddenly rushes down a slope.
senses.example: The photo showed the path where the avalanche had moved down the mountain.

senses.definition: A road or street, often a wide one in a town or city.
senses.example: We crossed the avenue at the traffic light.

senses.definition: A possible way to do or learn about something.
senses.example: The after-school club gave us another avenue for learning to code.

senses.definition: A number found by adding several amounts and dividing by how many amounts there are.
senses.example: The average of two and six is four.

senses.definition: Usual or close to what you would expect.
senses.example: On an average day, the walk takes about ten minutes.

senses.definition: To stay away from someone or something, or keep something from happening.
senses.example: We took the dry path to avoid the mud.

senses.definition: Not sleeping.
senses.example: I was awake before my alarm rang.

senses.definition: To wake up or cause someone to wake up.
senses.example: The first campers awoke at sunrise.

senses.definition: A prize or honor given for an achievement.
senses.example: Ravi got an award for helping new students.

senses.definition: To give someone something for an achievement or as the result of a decision.
senses.example: The judges will award the trophy on Saturday.

senses.definition: Knowing that something is happening or exists.
senses.example: I was not aware of the open window until the breeze blew in.

senses.definition: To a place farther from here, or not at the usual place.
senses.example: The bird flew away when the gate opened.

senses.definition: To or in a place where something is kept.
senses.example: Put your paints away when you have finished.

senses.definition: Very impressive or wonderful.
senses.example: That was an awesome drawing of the dragon.

senses.definition: So impressed or amazed that you stop and stare or cannot think of what to say.
senses.example: We stood awestruck when the huge whale rose out of the water.

senses.definition: Hard to move, use, or fit comfortably.
senses.example: The long package was awkward to carry on the bus.

senses.definition: Making you feel uncomfortable or unsure what to do.
senses.example: We had an awkward moment when we both reached for the last chair.

senses.definition: An imaginary or real line around which something turns.
senses.example: A spinning top turns around its axis.

senses.definition: A line on a graph along which values are marked and measured.
senses.example: The bottom axis shows the days of the week.

senses.definition: A rod on which a wheel turns or that turns with a wheel.
senses.example: The wheels of the toy truck spun around a metal axle.
